headline: Messi's Control Lesson Overwhelms Algeria's Pressing
story: Argentina seized this contest with ruthless efficiency despite surrendering 51 per cent possession. Lionel Messi orchestrated a 4-4-2 that bent Algeria's relentless high press into ineffectual chaos. An early goal at 17 minutes set the rhythm. When Algeria recovered possession, Argentina's ball-regain speed—18.4 seconds—suffocated any momentum. By the 60th-minute second goal, the contest was already decided; the press aggression had yielded only one shot on target from seven attempts.

The xG chasm told the fuller story: Argentina's 1.58 against Algeria's 0.41. Messi's 9.8 rating vindicated every pass—his distribution broke Algeria's shape repeatedly. Algeria's tactical intensity (6.6 high-press phases) generated volume but lacked precision. When De Paul and Nicolas Gonzalez combined in midfield, they exposed the void behind the press. A 76th-minute third goal confirmed Argentina had simply been the more cogent side.

keyMoment.text: Second goal (xG 0.63) exposed the futility of Algeria's relentless pressing.

home.verdict: Messi's efficiency transcended possession; Argentina dominated through press compactness.
points: Ball recovery at 18.4s was three seconds faster than Algeria's—press exhaustion reversed.
Forced 46 turnovers: vertical passes through midfield dismantled the high-press structure.
9.8 Messi rating: when one player operates at that level, possession becomes secondary.

away.verdict: Relentless pressing without payoff: intensity didn't breed precision.
points: Ball recovery of 20.2s left them chasing shadows; Messi exploited the open field.
Seven shots yielded only one on target: press chaos became attacking desperation.
Four-three-three midfield was overrun; De Paul controlled the tempo Argentina needed.

statLine: Pressing paradox: Algeria's 6.6 high-press phases generated seven shots and one on target. Argentina's 1.58 xG and Messi's 9.8 rating yielded three.
